title: Bulk-OUT receive path for root delivery: a variant of the NAT-041 DWC3 engine with one bulk-OUT endpoint (DEPCFG/DEPXFERCFG, chained TRBs of up to 16 MiB into the window, XferComplete handling, rx_bytes/rx_trbs/rx_errors in GET_INFO), its model, and a host sender (resumable by offset, bounded writes, checks rx_bytes); built under its own path without editing NAT-041
acceptance: Engine and model tests pass including seeded defects (short packet, TRB error, host disconnect mid-transfer, duplicate offset, wrong length) as NAT-041 did; endpoint and register values are cited to the pinned vendor driver or the Synopsys documentation named in NAT-041, not invented.

tools/ios/root_send.py sends a file to the model device by offset with a bounded write size, resumes after an injected failure, refuses a file whose size is not a multiple of 16 KiB, and prints the byte count the device reports; tests do not mirror the implementation.
A mutation pass over the receive state machine and the sender; survivors listed. No native run in this task; the first host-to-device rate is measured later (NAT-078).
